stories.title: The Lighthouse Keeper's Daughter
stories.synopsis: Mara wants her father to tell her the truth about 1887 without having to ask, but he would rather keep the lamp lit and the subject closed.

scenes.title: The storm glass
scenes.summary: The glass stays clear while the sea turns. She stops asking him and starts watching him.
scenes.content:
The glass had been clear all morning, which was how Mara knew her father was lying. He kept it on the sill of the lamp room where the light could get at it, a sealed bulb of water and crystals that was meant to cloud before weather, and it sat there as clear as a held breath while the sea went the colour of slate.

“It's a toy,” he said, when she asked. “Your grandmother's toy.” He did not look at it. He looked at the wick he was trimming, and the wick did not need trimming.

She had learned to read him the way she read the water: not by what moved, but by what refused to.

“Tobias saw a boat,” she said.

“Tobias sees a great many things.” The shears closed on nothing. “Go down and see to the bread.”

By four the glass had clouded, and he had not.

The sea had been grey since dawn, and the gulls kept to the lee of the tower as if they knew something the glass did not. He said nothing, which was its own kind of answer, and she filed it with the others.

She counted the steps the way her grandmother had taught her, not to know where she was but to keep her hands from shaking. The ledger lay open on the table, and the dates in it did not match the letters in the flour tin.

Below, the village lights came on one at a time, each one a small refusal of the dark. By the time the lamp was lit, the question had changed shape, and so had she.

speakers.name: Mara
speakers.want: to hear him admit the glass is clear because he needs it to be

speakers.name: Elias

speakers.unsaid: that he has seen the boat

dialogue.script:
MARA (pressing): It's clear.
ELIAS (correcting): It's a toy.
MARA (pressing): It was clear in March, too.
ELIAS (deflecting): Pass me the shears.
MARA (naming): You don't need the shears.
ELIAS (freezing out): …
MARA (retreating): Tobias saw a boat.
